reasons: R1 DEGENERATE: the only assessable load-bearing foundational requirement with any variation (order_record_resolves) has a per-case state that is a 1:1 recode of one corpus construction parameter (record_lookup_status). The aggregate value equals 1 - (record-unresolved slice fraction) by construction and cannot fail for a reason not baked into corpus sampling. This is the pattern docs/retired-figures.md item 2 retired.

R2 UNEXERCISABLE HEADLINE EXAMPLE: currency_integrity - the second requirement P3-D leans on - is DORMANT on 30/30 cases (every tool call and every orders.db row is INR) and is ORDINARY_CLAIM-shaped by the boundary test, not foundational.
R3 NON-COMPARABLE ACROSS TOOLS: issue_refund has 1 assessable requirement; tau2 has 0 assessable; send_document has 0. '100% (1/1)' and 'N/A (0/0)' are not the same kind of quantity.

R4 DENOMINATOR NOT INDEPENDENTLY ENUMERABLE: P3-A never listed order_record_resolves; P3-B found it for issue_refund only, by construction. The candidate set is an open lower bound, so the denominator is not a fixed population.

R5 MANIPULABLE: gaming tests B (remove the failing requirement -> 100%/N/A) and D (VIOLATED -> SATISFIED -> 100%) both move the metric with no change to case safety, and D is a defensible re-reading rather than an adversarial edit.

R6 CATEGORY INCOHERENT: the 6 candidates split across FOUNDATIONAL_REQUIREMENT (3, one of them NOT_ASSESSABLE), ORDINARY_CLAIM (1), ACTION_VALIDITY_CHECK (1), UNCLEAR (1). A single ratio would average over structurally different things.

cross_tool_comparability.finding: issue_refund has 1 assessable load-bearing foundational requirement; the tau2 family has 0 assessable (1 NOT_ASSESSABLE + 1 already-counted-by-P3-A binding gap); send_document has none. A percentage of '100% (1/1)' for issue_refund and 'N/A (0/0)' for tau2 and send_document are not comparable quantities - they do not answer the same question and cannot be ranked.
cross_tool_comparability.send_document_negative_control: bench/extraction_reference.py UNREPRESENTABLE_REQUIRED has NO entry for send_document; P3-D section 16 confirms its two required kinds are both bound and representable. A foundational-coverage % for send_document is 0/0 = N/A.

definition_of_foundational_requirement: A condition that (a) must hold before an action's claim-level verification is meaningful or possible, (b) is not an agent-attributable value-checkable assertion, (c) is evaluated on whether verification is possible rather than by comparing an asserted value to evidence, and (d) can make a set of downstream claims unevaluable at once. Operationally: a candidate is FOUNDATIONAL_REQUIREMENT only if the boundary_test answers are (agent_can_assert_value=false, evaluated_by_value_comparison=false, uses_normal_evidence_resolver=false, attributable_to_agent_assertion=false, gates_multiple_downstream_claims=true, prerequisite_for_interpreting_action=true). A candidate that can be asserted and is checked by value comparison is an ORDINARY_CLAIM missing a ClaimKind. A candidate that is a structural property of the tool call needing no evidence is an ACTION_VALIDITY_CHECK.

silent_pass.does_the_foundational_layer_expose_the_g: MARGINALLY. P1's per-case ledger already shows 4 claims as UNAVAILABLE with reason 'authoritative_lookup_empty'. The foundational layer names the single shared cause ('order_record_resolves: VIOLATED') instead of leaving it as an inference from 4 rows plus a receipt verdict (SOURCE_UNRELIABLE) and root_cause (evidence_below_reliability_floor) that both point at 'bad data' rather than 'absent record'. what_this_is: Falsification of the P3-D separate-foundational-layer recommendation and of a candidate foundational-requirement coverage percentage, over a frozen independently authored reference and the frozen 30-case P3-B issue_refund corpus. Deterministic; no model, no network.
